# Retired- and static-instruction baselines for the examples/bench corpus,
# checked against every run by scripts/ci-check-perf.
#
# FORMAT: metric  value  [tolerance%]. The metric key is
# <arch>/<benchmark>.<text|ir> — .text is the count of instructions in the
# emitted assembly, .ir the count of instructions actually retired.
#
# WHAT IS EXACT AND WHAT IS NOT. Every figure here repeats to the digit on a
# given commit EXCEPT `map_string.ir`: core/map draws a per-process
# string-hash seed (#6194), which moves probe lengths. Measured spread over
# seven runs: 156,124,457 .. 156,922,358, i.e. 0.51%. That one line therefore
# carries an explicit 2% tolerance and is baselined at the middle of the
# range rather than at a sample. `map_int.ir` is exact — the seed is consulted
# for string keys only — and is deliberately left on the default so the two
# together show which half of a map regression moved.
#
# Everything else uses the 1% default, which flags a change of one part in a
# hundred. That is a significance threshold, not a noise floor: the numbers
# have no noise.
#
# ADVISORY, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — see scripts/ci-check-perf. When a number
# moves on purpose, update it in the same PR; the job summary prints the
# corrected lines ready to paste. Keep the reason in the PR, not here.
#
# TWO ARCHITECTURES. An instruction count is not comparable across ISAs, so the
# keys are namespaced by arch and compared independently — and each job compares
# only its OWN namespace, so an x86_64 entry is not a missing measurement on the
# aarch64 runner.

x86_64/array_append.text	511

# aarch64, the arch this project defaults to. The `.ir` half comes from the
# Perf workflow's own perf-aarch64 job, because no aarch64 host is available to
# the dev container — paste its block in verbatim. The `.text` half is a line
# count over `fern -target arm64-linux` output and so is host-independent: a
# cross-compile here reproduces the runner's figure exactly, which is how these
# are kept current. map_string.ir carries the same 2% the x86_64 twin does, for
# the same per-process hash seed.
#
# Do NOT extrapolate an aarch64 figure from its x86_64 twin: the ratio is not
# constant. Over `.text` it runs from 0.85 (call_overhead) to 1.18
# (utf8_ingest_unchecked) — one ISA emitting fewer instructions than the other
# on one program says nothing about the next. A new benchmark reports as
# UNBASELINED here for one CI run, which is the gate saying "measured,
# recorded, not yet compared" — paste that run's block in rather than guessing.
